findings.title: Dynamic imports are all started eagerly, defeating lazy loading
findings.body: Every value in the appStore object literal is an already-invoked import() call, so importing this module immediately starts loading all 28 app packages and their dependencies, even when the caller only needs one app. This defeats the intended on-demand loading, and because most of these promises are never awaited for a given request, a rejection from an unused optional app can surface as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being handled by the code that selected that app. Store lazy thunks such as () => import(...) or otherwise create the import only for the requested key.

findings.title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited and outside try/catch
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) returns immediately, so Reschedule proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before getCalendar and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting finish. Rejections from the async callback are not caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections, and on serverless runtimes the deletions may never complete after the response returns. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) so deletions finish and errors are handled before continuing.

findings.title: Async forEach races reschedule email/webhook against booking deletions
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) is not awaited, so the requestReschedule mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and webhooks while calendar/video deletion for the old booking is still pending at the dynamic-import step. The deletions can be lost if execution is frozen after the mutation returns, and failures become unhandled rejections rather than being surfaced or logged. Await Promise.all over a map of the deletion operations before sending the email/webhooks.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is awaited
findings.body: The recurring-cancellation branch uses credentials.forEach(async ...) and pushes into apiDeletes only after awaiting getCalendar and calendar.deleteEvent. Because the forEach is never awaited, the handler reaches Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at the end (and the earlier await apiDeletes in the paid path) before those pushes happen, so recurring calendar events are not reliably deleted before attendee/booking-reference rows are removed and the cancellation response is sent. Replace the forEach with an awaited for...of loop or await Promise.all(map(...)) that fills apiDeletes before it is consumed.
